grand_strategy.reading:
Afghanistan under the Taliban is the pariah that outlasts its isolators.
The Emirate has no allies, no UN seat and a ruling circle indicted by the
ICC, and yet by October 2026 it is courted by Moscow (recognition, a
military-technical agreement), Beijing, Delhi, Riyadh, Doha and even
Brussels and Berlin. Luttwak's lamp shows why: it is useful against worse
enemies (the Islamic State in Khorasan) and it holds what everybody needs
(transit, water, minerals, a land bridge between Central and South Asia),
so each power that would isolate it has a competing reason to deal with it.
The strategy is to sell access without surrendering the social order,
which is why Zelin calls it recognition without concessions.
The weakness is the relation that used to protect it. The Pakistani
patron became the main military enemy over the TTP, and the paradox is
Luttwakian in the pure sense: loyalty to the movement's sister
organisation costs the Emirate its border, its main port route and, in
February 2026, air raids on Kandahar itself. Kabul now builds a ring of
alternatives (Iran, Central Asia, India, the Gulf, Russia) but every
ring has a price: Iranian dependence and expulsions, a water quarrel with
Uzbekistan, a Tajik neighbour hosting the Panjshir resistance. Two signals
that are not rows: Khalilzad's presence at the Saudi gas signing on
7 Sep 2026, which the State Department disowned, and the Moscow Format of
5 Oct 2026, where Pakistani and Taliban envoys traded accusations in the
same room. The open question for the next year is whether the Gulf and
Chinese mediators can turn the strikes into a settlement on the TTP before
the Emirate's hold on the north-east frays.

stances.note: Pakistan was the Taliban's patron and sanctuary; since 9 Oct 2025 (first Pakistani strike on Kabul) it is the Emirate's main military enemy: border war in October 2025, Doha/Istanbul ceasefire talks that failed, 'open war' declared by Khawaja Asif on 26-27 Feb 2026 with strikes on Kabul and Kandahar, a truce from 18 Mar, talks in Urumqi in April, new strikes on 24 Sep 2026; borders mostly closed since 12 Oct 2025; over 2.4 million Afghans returned from Pakistan since 2023. Zelin (WINEP, Aug 2026) says Pakistan went 'from patron to adversary' - a source that uses the stronger word. Adversary test: the grade stays rival because neither side's declared aim is the other's disappearance. Islamabad says borders reopen on 'decisive and verifiable action' against the TTP and keeps attending China-, Qatar-, Turkey- and Saudi-mediated talks; Kabul says it is 'open to talks', sends delegations, and treats the TTP as Pakistan's internal affair. Asif's 'obliterate' and 'open war' lines and the Taliban's claim that Pakistan backs anti-Taliban fronts are the argument for adversary and are the reason the trend is cooling and the confidence C; if Pakistan states a regime-change aim or Kabul seeks Pakistani territory, regrade. Bond - grievance: the TTP sanctuary, deportations, the Durand Line, the trade closures. Asymmetric pairing with PAK's own side is expected to differ (Islamabad is likely to grade Kabul adversary).
